layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Panoramic video generation aims to synthesize 360-degree immersive videos,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: holding significant importance in the fields of VR, world models, and spatial in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: telligence. Existing works fail to synthesize high-quality panoramic videos due

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the inherent modality gap between panoramic data and perspective data, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constitutes the majority of the training data for modern diffusion models. In this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paper, we propose a novel framework utilizing pretrained perspective video models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for generating panoramic videos. Specifically, we design a novel panorama rep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resentation named ViewPoint map, which possesses global spatial continuity and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine-grained visual details simultaneously. With our proposed Pano-Perspective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attention mechanism, the model benefits from pretrained perspective priors and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: captures the panoramic spatial correlations of the ViewPoint map effectively. Ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tensive experiments demonstrate that our method can synthesize highly dynamic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Imagine you're traveling—would you seize the chance to capture the breathtaking landscapes that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unfold before you? When you return home, do you long to relive and immerse yourself in those

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vivid experiences once more? Recently, omnidirectional vision has garnered increasing attention

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as it unlocks immersive AR/VR, virtual travel, and telepresence experiences. However, recording

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 360-degree videos requires expensive professional devices, i.e., 360 cameras, making the creation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: panoramic content challenging, and most consumers capture only narrow field-of-view (FoV) clips

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on portable monocular cameras, e.g., smartphones. Enabling these perspective recordings to become

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: full panoramas would democratize spherical media, letting anyone relive or share memories in true

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 360-degree form.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Achieving this conversion is non-trivial due to fundamental representation gaps between perspective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and panorama domains. A straightforward approach is to adopt the widely-used Equirectangular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Projection (ERP) for panoramas, which maps the spherical view onto a rectangular image. Unfortu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nately, this format introduces severe distortions, especially near the poles, stretching and squashing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content unnaturally. More critically, equirectangular images lie outside the distribution of typical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training data for modern generative models, which are at the center of the recent surge of interest in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computer vision and pattern recognition [45, 27, 28, 42, 41, 19–24]. Diffusion models [10, 29, 32]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and VAEs [14] are predominantly trained on perspective imagery, so without significant adaptation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: they struggle to produce high-quality results in the warped ERP space. On the other hand, one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: could represent the panorama as multiple perspective projections. A common choice is the Cubemap

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Projection(CP) format, which unfolds the sphere into six faces (each a 90° FOV perspective view).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The CP representation avoids polar distortions and yields locally planar patches well-aligned with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the priors of convolutional and diffusion networks. However, a naive cubemap suffers from spatial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: discontinuities at the borders of the faces. The six faces are disjoint on a 2D grid, making it difficult

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for a neural model to capture cross-face consistency. In short, existing representations force a trade-off

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between continuity and distortion: ERP offers end-to-end continuity but distorts the content, whereas

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CP preserves local fidelity but fragments the panoramic space. Neither is ideal for generative video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modeling, especially when temporal consistency is also required.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we address the above-mentioned issues by introducing ViewPoint, a novel 360° video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: representation and generation framework that bridges the strengths of ERP and CP. At the core of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ViewPoint is a spatially-aware pseudo-stitching scheme that reprojects and rearranges the scene into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an overlapping set of perspective views with greatly improved continuity. Specifically, we first convert

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the panorama into six cube faces—each a distortion-free perspective view—and then merge them

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into a small number of overlapping "pseudo-perspective" panels. Because these panels share content

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: along their boundaries, they eliminate the hard seams of a standard cubemap while remaining fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compatible with existing 2D diffusion models. On this representation, the proposed Pano-Perspective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attention delivers two key benefits: (1) Global coherence: Pano-attention blocks span the entire

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stitched map (and time), ensuring that opposite directions align and the scene stays consistent. (2)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Local fidelity: Perspective-attention blocks focus on each panel's neighborhood, preserving fine

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: texture, color, and motion details. With this attention mechanism, we take full advantage of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generative capabilities of diffusion models and adapt them to the task of panoramic video generation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where high-quality data is scarce.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In summary, our contributions are as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We introduce a novel representation for 360-degree content aimed at improving spatial continuity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and reducing distortion while leveraging the power of diffusion models to generate 360-degree

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: videos through the proposed format.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We design a Pano-Perspective attention mechanism, enabling the model to simultaneously maintain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: global spatial continuity across the entire panorama and significantly enhance the preservation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine-grained details and motion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method can generate high-quality 360-degree videos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and achieve state-of-the-art performance, outperforming previous approaches.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Related Works

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Panorama Representations. Panoramic images are often projected from spherical space to the 2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plane for processing and storage [1]. Equirectangular Projection (ERP) is the most popular format,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which uniformly maps pixels from a spherical surface to a planar rectangle. Despite its simplicity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and spatial continuity, ERP inevitably brings disadvantages such as geometric distortion at the poles.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cubemap Projection (CP), on the other hand, projects panoramas to six cube faces with the FoV of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to alleviate geometric distortion. However, under this representation, only one cube face is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explicitly spatially continuous with its four adjacent faces on the 2D plane.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Panorama Generation. Panoramic image generation [13, 34, 40, 44, 8, 6, 18, 46, 38, 30, 37, 15]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aims to synthesize 360-degree immersive images based on user-provided textual or visual clues. It

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires the generated images to be seamless in spherical space while maintaining rationality in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: any perspective anchor. Recent studies [13, 34, 40, 44, 46, 38, 37, 15] leverage powerful image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diffusion models to generate high-quality panoramic images. Benefiting from the great generative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capabilities of diffusion models, these works have made significant advancements in omnidirectional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image synthesis. Among them, PanoGen [15] achieves high-quality results in indoor scenarios

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by introducing a recursive outpainting and stitching mechanism. PanFusion [46] proposes a dual-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branch pipeline to integrate equirectangular features and perspective features. CubeDiff [13] uses an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alternative representation, cubemap, to synthesize panoramic images with high fidelity and diversity.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Despite the significant progress in omnidirectional image generation, achieving similar success in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: field of video remains a challenging problem, as it requires spatial-temporal consistency across the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entire spherical space, as well as costly computational resources.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A few works [39, 16, 25, 33] explore panoramic video generation. 4K4DGEN [16] animates a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: given high-resolution panoramic image through user intention. However, the requirement of high-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quality panoramic inputs limits the application scenarios, as it struggles to generate omnidirectional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content without the given images. VidPanos [25] extends a given video to a larger FoV by using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Temporal Coarse-to-Fine and Spatial Aggregation strategies, but it does not produce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FoV

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: panoramas. 360DVD [39] trains a 360-Adapter to exploit the generative capabilities of text-to-video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diffusion models, achieving text-driven 360-degree video generation. Most relevant to our work,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Imagine360 [33] utilizes a dual-branch design, similar to [46], to synthesize panoramic videos from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: given perspective inputs. However, the equirectangular videos generated by both 360DVD [39] and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Imagine360 [33] exhibit severe distortion, especially at the poles, significantly degrading the sense of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: immersion and realism. We argue that the spatial distortion and motion drifting caused by ERP make

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it difficult for models to effectively understand the polar regions with limited training data. After all,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generating perspective videos with extreme motion is still a challenge, let alone panoramas.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Current video generation models employ 3D positional encodings, enabling them to uniformly model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: videos across both spatial and temporal dimensions. Building on this foundation, open-source video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models, such as Wan 2.1 [35] and CogVideoX [43], have acquired rich generative capabilities by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training on extensive datasets of perspective videos. Multi-view generation approaches represent a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: panoramic video as a collection of multiple perspective videos. Although these perspective views

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: align well with the native generative capabilities of video models, the spatial relationships between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: them are only inferred implicitly. This is typically achieved by introducing extra positional encodings

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or by constructing partial overlaps between adjacent faces. Such methods, however, tend to disrupt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the model's inherent generative abilities and introduce artifacts like color discrepancies and visible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seams in the resulting panoramic videos. Consequently, they fail to meet the demand for high-quality

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: panoramic video generation. In contrast, an intact panoramic representation can naturally align with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the native 3D attention mechanism of DiTs. In this paradigm, the model is able to capture global

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information across the entire panoramic scene, leading to the generation of superior panoramic videos.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our proposed ViewPoint Map is precisely such an explicit panoramic representation. It projects the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: non-Euclidean spherical data onto a single, unified Euclidean plane. This provides global continuity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and allows the model to "see" the entire spherical space in a single pass.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Video Outpainting. Formally, extending from a given perspective view to a panoramic video is a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: kind of video outpainting task. Benefiting from pretrained diffusion models [10, 31, 29, 9], previous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: works [36, 5] have made notable progress in perspective video outpainting. However, due to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scarcity of 360-degree video data and the modality gap introduced by its unique representation form,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: panoramic video outpainting remains an open question. In this paper, we design a novel panorama

layout_dets.text: 4.1 Implementation Details

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Datasets & Preprocess. Our model is trained on 4 panorama datasets, including one image dataset,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Flickr360 [3], and three video datasets, WEB360 [39], ODV360 [3], and 360+x [4]. Among them,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: three datasets, generating corresponding descriptive captions. All datasets are resized to a resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , and during training, video data is divided into clips of 49 frames each.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Training. We first inflate the patch embedding layer of the powerful video generation model,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Wan2.1 [35], from 16 to 33 channels to accommodate the input data, and then fine-tune the entire

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model. The training process is executed on 8 × NVIDIA A100 GPUs, using a batch size of 1 and a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning rate of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . We employ a joint image-video training strategy, treating images as videos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with only one frame.

layout_dets.text: 4.2 Qualitative Comparison

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We compare our approach with three previous methods, including one perspective video outpainting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Imagine360 [33]. Adopting equirectangular representation, both 360DVD [39] and Imagine360 [33]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while the ground shows "swirls". We argue that these artifacts are caused by the model's difficulty

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in handling the spatial-temporal distortion introduced by ERP, as a slight movement can result in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significant disturbances at the poles.

layout_dets.text: The visualization of the comparison results is shown Fig. 5, where we present the ERP format

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: To demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, we conduct ablation experiments on panorama

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all Perspective blocks with the intact Pano blocks.

layout_dets.text: 6 Limitations and Future Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A significant challenge in panoramic video generation is achieving high resolution. Immersive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applications such as virtual reality (VR) necessitate ultra-high resolutions (e.g., 8K, 16K) to deliver

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a realistic and compelling user experience. However, current pre-trained diffusion models are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computationally constrained and cannot directly synthesize content at such scales. Consequently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in line with established practices, our work employs a two-stage generate-then-upscale pipeline to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mitigate this limitation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Looking ahead, our future work will focus on two primary directions. First, we aim to explore

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: NeurIPS Paper Checklist

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Claims

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paper's contributions and scope?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [Yes]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: The abstract and introduction clearly state the claims we made.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: made in the paper.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A No or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NA answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are not attained by the paper.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Limitations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [Yes]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: We discuss the limitations in the supplemental material.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the paper has no limitation while the answer No means that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors are encouraged to create a separate "Limitations" section in their paper.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: implications would be.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: technical jargon.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and how they scale with dataset size.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: address problems of privacy and fairness.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limitations that aren't acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an impor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tant role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Theory assumptions and proofs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a complete (and correct) proof?

layout_dets.text: Answer: [NA]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include theoretical results.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: referenced.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proof sketch to provide intuition.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. Experimental result reproducibility

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: Ours results is reproducible, and we will release the codes.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include experiments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If the paper includes experiments, a No answer to this question will not be perceived

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whether the code and data are provided or not.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to make their results reproducible or verifiable.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: appropriate to the research performed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nature of the contribution. For example

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to reproduce that algorithm.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the architecture clearly and fully.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the dataset).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. Open access to data and code

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instruc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: material?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [No]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: We will release the codes and weights, but not now as we are still in the process

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of organizing them.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that paper does not include experiments requiring code.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines (https://nips.cc/

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy) for more details.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: possible, so “No" is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: benchmark).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines (https :

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: //nips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy) for more details.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should state which ones are omitted from the script and why.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: versions (if applicable).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6. Experimental setting/details

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyper-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer, etc.) necessary to understand the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include experiments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: material.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7. Experiment statistical significance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information about the statistical significance of the experiments?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [No]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: The methodologies employed in this work involve computational models that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yield consistent and repeatable outputs without variability under the same conditions. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tests are based on established simulations that deterministically produce the same results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each time they are run, provided the input parameters remain unchanged

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include experiments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should answer "Yes" if the results are accompanied by error bars, confi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the main claims of the paper.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: run with given experimental conditions).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the mean.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of Normality of errors is not verified.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g. negative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: error rates).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, The authors should explain in the text how

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 8. Experiments compute resources

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: puter resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the experiments?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [Yes]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include experiments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: didn't make it into the paper).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 9. Code of ethics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [Yes]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: We understand the importance of ethical standards in research and take this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matter seriously.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If the authors answer No, they should explain the special circumstances that require a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deviation from the Code of Ethics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consid-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 10. Broader impacts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: societal impacts of the work performed?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [Yes]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: We discuss the potential societal impacts of our work in the supplemental

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: material.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that there is no societal impact of the work performed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If the authors answer NA or No, they should explain why their work has no societal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impact or why the paper does not address societal impact.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generate deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models that generate Deepfakes faster.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 11. Safeguards

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pretrained language models,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image generators, or scraped datasets)?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Answer: [Yes]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Justification: We commit to continuously monitoring the usage of our released models and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: codes and will take action to restrict access or provide additional guidance if we identify

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concerning patterns of misuse.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Guidelines:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The answer NA means that the paper poses no such risks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: safety filters.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: faith effort.

layout_dets.text: • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to

layout_dets.text: 9 Limitations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As shown in Fig. 10, the panoramic videos generated by our model contain watermarks, exhibit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mosaic artifacts on human faces, and occasionally reveal photographic equipment such as selfie sticks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the D regions of the video, which can degrade the immersive experience. These limitations can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attributed to the presence of watermarks and specialized post-processing in our training data [4, 39].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Specifically, 360 camera manufacturers typically embed their logos into the recorded videos, leading

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to an abundance of watermarked content within the dataset. In addition, some works [4] choose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to apply a mosaic effect to human faces in the datasets for ethical and moral considerations. We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: acknowledge and respect the ethical considerations taken by the creators of the datasets. We argue

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that these limitations can be addressed by using higher-quality datasets, where high quality refers to,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for example, removing watermarks or hiding photographic equipment through algorithms, as well as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: filtering out video clips containing human faces.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 10 Potential Societal Impact

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Panoramic video generation has the potential to bring significant positive societal impact. It can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: empower non-expert users to create high-quality immersive content, thereby fostering innovation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in digital art, virtual tourism, education, and cultural heritage preservation. This technology also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhance remote experiences and contributes to accessibility, enabling broader participation in virtual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environments for individuals with physical or economic limitations. Furthermore, it offers valuable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: support in scientific visualization and educational applications, especially in fields such as geography

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and urban planning. However, generating virtual panoramas also pose several challenges. Concerns

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: around privacy and ethics arise when real-world data containing personal identities are used for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training. The potential for misuse, including the creation of deepfakes and misleading visual content,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: raises serious issues regarding misinformation and public trust. Additionally, copyright infringement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and labor displacement in creative industries are growing concerns. To mitigate these risks, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is essential to implement robust regulatory frameworks, ethical guidelines, and public awareness

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: campaigns that promote responsible use and transparency in AI-driven content generation.
